data.cultural_impact: The name "Hadhansh" carries a rich cultural legacy in Hinduism. Arrangements such as naming ceremonies or thread-wearing ceremonies (Upanayana) are often held where the infant is blessed with sacred mantras, including the name "Hadhansh." This name also holds special significance during various Hindu festivals like Diwali, where prayers and rituals are performed for the Lord of Wealth, to seek his blessings for financial prosperity.
data.spiritual_significance: Within Hindu spiritual thought, "Hadhansh" signifies the divine presence of Lord Vishnu, who is believed to bestow prosperity and well-being upon his devotees. Those who carry this name are thought to be under the protective grace of the Lord, invoking spiritual blessings and prosperity in all aspects of life. Like a wave that crests and surges forth with power and promise, the name "Hadhansh" invokes a sense of spiritual prowess that has the potential to ride the tide of life's ups and downs.

historical_references.reference: The Hadhansh were an important branch of the Yadava dynasty of the Deccan, ruling in the region around the present-day city of Davangere in Karnataka from the 12th to the 15th century.
The Hadhansh were also known as the Alamalai Nayakas, a feudatory dynasty who ruled over parts of the Chola Empire in Tamil Nadu during the 13th and 14th centuries.
